order: say someone is in the water and where
keep watching them, and do what the helper says
safety: keep watching the person while you call

little.skill: Water rules, and help from the side
little.twist: Your ball floats away into the deep water, and the float doesn't glow.
little.can_now: follow the water rules and help from the side: shout for help, throw a float, never jump in

steps.say: The practice pool. Gus the lifeguard is watching. This is practice: let's learn the water rules together.
Before you go near water, who must be with you?

choices.why: Never by yourself: a grown-up watches you near water, every time.
Friends are fun, but a grown-up must watch too.

steps.done: A grown-up watches, every time.

steps.say: The floor by the pool is wet. How do you move?

choices.why: Wet floors are slippery. Walk, never run.

steps.done: Walk, never run.

steps.say: Your ball floats away into the deep water. What do you do?

choices.text: Ask a grown-up to get it
Lean over and reach for it
choices.why: Leaning over the water you can slip in. A grown-up gets it.
Never go in after a toy. A grown-up helps.

steps.done: A grown-up gets it with the long pole.

steps.say: Bobo is going on a boat. Help him put on his life jacket: it helps him float.
steps.done: It's on. Now click the buckle.

steps.say: Click the buckle shut.
steps.done: Click! Snug and safe.

steps.say: Oh! Pip-pop slipped in at the deep end and can't get out. Never jump in to help: even grown-ups help from the side with a float. Let's do it.
First, shout for help: touch Gus the lifeguard.
steps.done: Gus is coming! Help Pip-pop from the side.

steps.say: Throw the float to Pip-pop. Aim just past her, so it lands by her hands.
steps.done: It landed by her. She's holding on!

steps.say: Throw the float to Pip-pop, by yourself.
steps.done: Right by her hands!

steps.say: Hold the rope and pull her gently to the side. Stay back from the edge.
steps.done: She's at the side. Gus helps her out.

steps.say: Pip-pop is out and smiling. You stayed on the side and threw a float: that's how to help.
Water rules: a grown-up watching, walk don't run, a life jacket on boats, and help from the side: shout, throw, never jump in.

check.say: Who must watch you near water?
Someone is in the water and can't get out. What do you do?
What helps you float on a boat?

name_it.title: Water rules
lines: A grown-up watching, every time you're near water.
Walk, never run, by the pool.
A life jacket on boats and in open water.
Someone in trouble? Shout for help and throw something that floats.
name_it.source: The Royal Life Saving Society, the RNLI and the WHO's drowning prevention advice

little.try_real: With a grown-up at a pool or a beach: find the lifeguard, the safety signs and a float that could be thrown.

sources.fact: Children near water need a grown-up watching them, close by, all the time; drowning is quick and quiet.
To help someone in the water: shout for help, reach or throw something that floats from the side, never go in after them.
sources.source: Royal Life Saving Society UK, water safety

sources.fact: Life jackets help you float; wear one on boats and around open water.
Walk, don't run, on wet pool surrounds: they are slippery.
sources.source: Royal Life Saving Society UK, swimming pool safety

middle.skill: Spot trouble, rips and life jackets
middle.twist: The quiet friend could be anywhere, the rip pulls the other way, and nothing glows.
middle.can_now: spot someone in trouble in the water, help from the side, swim out of a rip current and check a life jacket's fit

steps.say: The practice pool and the practice beach. Today: spotting someone in trouble, rip currents, and a life jacket's fit.

not.pip_wave: Pip-pop is waving and laughing: she's playing. Look for someone quiet and upright.
not.bobo_splash: Bobo is splashing and shouting for fun. Someone in trouble often can't shout.
not.kiki_float: Kiki is floating happily on her back, kicking. Look again.

steps.say: One friend needs help. Look carefully: someone in trouble in the water is often quiet.
steps.done: Yes: Mo is upright, head back, mouth at the water, not waving. That can mean trouble.

not.pip_wave: Pip-pop is waving and laughing: she's playing.
not.bobo_splash: Bobo is splashing for fun. Someone in trouble often can't shout.
not.kiki_float: Kiki is floating happily on her back.

steps.say: One friend needs help. Who is it?
steps.done: Mo: quiet, upright, not waving. You spotted it by yourself.

steps.say: What do you do first?

choices.why: Shout straight away: help needs to come fast.

steps.done: The lifeguard is on the way. Help from the side meanwhile.

safe_mistake.why: Someone in trouble in the water grabs anything, even a helper, so a helper who jumps in needs help too.
safe_mistake.right: Help from the side: reach with the pole, or throw something that floats. Never go in after them.

steps.say: Mo is near the side and can't get out. Help her!
steps.done: The pole, from the side: safe for you and for Mo.

steps.say: Lie down or kneel at the edge, so she can't pull you in.
steps.done: Low and steady.

steps.say: Hold the pole out to Mo and keep it still while she grabs it.
steps.done: She's holding on.

steps.say: Pull her in slowly to the side.
steps.done: At the side! The lifeguard helps her out.

steps.say: Now the practice beach. Lifeguards put up red and yellow flags.

not.rip_water: That calm-looking gap in the waves can be a rip current. Swim between the flags.

steps.say: Where is the safest place to swim? Touch it.
steps.done: Between the red and yellow flags: the lifeguards watch there.

steps.say: Practice time: you're swimming with a body board, and a rip current gently pulls you out. See the arrows: the water flows out to sea.
Practice time: you're swimming with a body board, and a rip current gently pulls you out. Watch which way the water flows.

safe_mistake.wrong: swimming straight back against a rip current
safe_mistake.why: A rip current flows out to sea faster than you can swim, so swimming straight back against it only makes you tired.
safe_mistake.right: Swim along the beach, out of the rip, then back to the shore.

steps.say: Which way do you swim?
steps.done: Along the beach: out of the rip!

safe_mistake.wrong: swimming straight back against a rip current
safe_mistake.why: A rip current flows out to sea faster than you can swim, so swimming straight back against it only makes you tired.
safe_mistake.right: Swim along the beach, out of the rip, then back to the shore.

steps.say: This rip pulls the other way. Which way do you swim?
steps.done: Along the beach, the other way: out!

steps.say: Now swim back in to the shore, away from the rip.
steps.done: Safe on the sand.

steps.say: Now back in to the shore.
steps.done: Safe on the sand.

steps.say: If you can't swim out of a rip, what do you do?

choices.text: Float, raise one hand and shout
Swim against it as hard as you can
choices.why: That tires you out. Float and wave: lifeguards will come.

steps.done: Float and wave for help.

steps.say: Pip-pop is going in a boat. Help her put on her life jacket and buckle it.
steps.done: On and buckled.

steps.say: Check the fit: lift it gently at the shoulders. It should stay down, not ride up past her chin.
steps.done: It stays down: a good fit.

steps.say: You can spot someone in trouble, help from the side, swim out of a rip, and check a life jacket.

check.say: Someone in trouble in the water is often...

choices.text: Quiet: they can't wave or shout

check.say: Your friend can't get out of the water. You...

choices.text: Reach or throw from the side

check.say: A rip current pulls you out. You swim...
Where do you swim at the beach?

choices.text: Between the red and yellow flags
Stays down when lifted at the shoulders

name_it.title: Spot it, reach it, swim out of a rip
lines: Someone in trouble in the water is often quiet: they can't wave or shout.
Shout for help. Reach or throw from the side: never go in after them.
Swim between the red and yellow flags.
Caught in a rip: swim along the beach, then in. Can't? Float, raise a hand and shout.
A life jacket that fits stays down when you lift it at the shoulders.
name_it.source: The RNLI, the Royal Life Saving Society, the US National Weather Service (rip currents) and the US Coast Guard (life jackets)

middle.try_real: At the beach with a grown-up: find the lifeguards' red and yellow flags and talk about where a rip could be. Check your own life jacket's fit together.

sources.fact: Drowning usually looks quiet: the person is upright, head back or low, mouth at the water, can't wave or call out (the instinctive drowning response).
sources.source: Pia, F., 'Observations on the drowning of nonswimmers' (1974); US Coast Guard, On Scene (2006)

sources.fact: If caught in a rip: don't swim against it; swim parallel to the shore until free, then head back in; if you can't, float, raise a hand and shout.
Break the grip of the rip: swim along the shoreline, out of the current, then swim at an angle back to shore.
sources.source: US National Weather Service, rip current safety

sources.fact: Swim between the red and yellow flags: the area lifeguards watch.
A life jacket should fit snugly: buckled, and when lifted at the shoulders it should not ride up past the chin or ears.
sources.source: US Coast Guard Boating Safety, life jackets

sources.fact: Reach or throw from the side; a helper who goes in can get into trouble too.

big.twist: Which way out of the hole? You choose, and nothing glows.
big.can_now: stay off thin ice, get out if they fall in (still, arms out, kick, roll, crawl) and help from the bank

steps.say: The practice pond in winter. This is practice: today, ice and cold water.
The pond is frozen. Can you walk on it?

choices.why: You can't tell how thick ice is by looking. Stay off ponds, lakes and rivers.
Ice near the edge is often the thinnest. Stay off.

steps.done: Stay off the ice: you can't see how thick it is.

steps.say: Let's practise what to do if you ever fall through. You're in the cold water at the edge of the hole. It's only practice.
Cold water takes your breath away. Keep still for a moment and let your breathing calm down.
steps.done: Calmer. The first shock passes in about a minute.

steps.say: Turn back the way you came: the ice there held you.
Which way do you climb out?

choices.text: The far side: it looks closer
choices.why: You know the ice you walked on held you. Turn back towards it.

steps.done: Back the way you came.

steps.say: Put both arms out flat on the ice.
steps.done: Arms out wide on the ice.

steps.say: Kick your legs hard, like swimming, and slide forward onto the ice. Push four times.
steps.done: You slid out onto the ice!

steps.say: Stay flat on the ice: lie down.
steps.done: Flat: your weight is spread out.

safe_mistake.why: Standing puts all your weight on one small spot, and the ice can break again. Lying flat spreads your weight out.
safe_mistake.right: Stay flat: roll away from the hole, then crawl.

steps.say: Roll away from the hole.
steps.done: Rolled away from the hole.

steps.say: Crawl back the way you came, to the bank. Stay low.
steps.done: On the bank!

steps.say: Now back to the bank, the safe way.
steps.done: On the bank, by yourself!

steps.say: You can stand up now. Get warm: wrap up in the blanket, get into dry clothes, and tell a grown-up.
steps.done: Warm and dry. A grown-up calls {number} so a doctor can check you.

steps.say: Practice again: now Mo has fallen through the ice near the bank.
What do you do first?

choices.why: Stay where you can see Mo and get help now: shout and call {number}.

steps.done: Help is coming. Tell Mo: keep still, arms on the ice.

safe_mistake.wrong: walking onto the ice to help
safe_mistake.why: The ice that broke under Mo can break under you too: then two people need help.
safe_mistake.right: Stay on the bank: lie down and reach out with a long branch or a pole. Never walk on the ice to help.

steps.say: Help Mo!
steps.done: From the bank, with a long branch: safe for you.

steps.say: Lie down on the bank, so you can't be pulled in.
steps.done: Low on the bank.

steps.say: Hold the branch out to Mo and keep it still.
steps.done: She's holding on.

steps.say: Pull her slowly to the bank.
steps.done: Mo is out! Wrap her in a blanket while help comes.

steps.say: Stay off the ice. Fell in? Keep still, arms out, kick, roll and crawl. To help: from the bank, never walk on the ice.

check.say: Can you walk on a frozen pond?
You fell through the ice. First...

choices.text: Keep still and get your breath
Splash hard to get out fast

check.say: To get out onto the ice...
On the ice after falling in, you...
Your friend falls through the ice. You...

choices.text: Call for help and reach from the bank

name_it.title: Thin ice and cold water
lines: Stay off frozen ponds, lakes and rivers.
Fell in? Keep still for a minute while your breathing calms.
Arms out on the ice, kick, slide out, then roll and crawl.
Never stand up until you are back on the bank.
Someone else in? Call {number} and reach from the bank: never walk on the ice.
name_it.source: The RNLI and the Royal Life Saving Society (Float to Live, ice safety), and national ice safety advice

big.try_real: With a grown-up in winter: find the warning signs by a frozen pond or lake, and say the steps aloud together: still, arms out, kick, roll, crawl.

sources.fact: Stay off frozen ponds, lakes and rivers: you can't tell how thick the ice is.
sources.source: Royal Life Saving Society UK, ice safety

sources.fact: Cold water shock takes your breath away; it passes in about a minute: keep still and float until your breathing calms (Float to Live).
Fallen through ice: turn towards the way you came, put your arms on the unbroken ice, kick to slide out, roll away from the hole, crawl back; don't stand until you're on solid ground.
sources.source: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources, ice safety

sources.fact: To help someone through ice: call the emergency number, stay off the ice, reach with a long object or throw something from the bank, lying down.
sources.source: Royal Life Saving Society UK, ice safety
